newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen falls on Sakakibara's comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen falls on Sakakibara's comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen eased in late Wednesday trade, dampened by a Japan finance ministry official's comments on recent yen movements.

In a speech to currency dealers, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's international finance bureau, said the yen's recent decline against the dollar was clearly excessive and Japan would take decisive action at an appropriate time.
Dealers said his comments on political pressure to raise the official discount rate, although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan (BOJ), ignited rate hike fears.

"Euroyen was firmer until his speech. The market was confident BOJ would not raise the rate despite unhappiness among some politicians about Japan's low rates," a dealer said. "But now, the confidence has been shaken."
After hitting a high at 99.14, December Euroyen fell to 99.06 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close of 99.12. Turnover was around 11,135 lots.
Euroyen was earlier boosted by the BOJ's unexpected respite from its regular morning operations, dealers said.

The respite, which left about 200 billion yen surplus in the market, coupled with Tuesday's lower than expected drainage, was seen as a signal BOJ would maintain an accommodative money policy and keep interest rates low.
BOJ left a surplus in the market on Tuesday, draining only 400 billion against a 510 billion yen surplus.

Short-covering in the June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures after Euroyen hit its 99.13 resistance pushed JGB to a high of 127.00. June JGB finally settled at 126.57 on a meagre volume of 172 lots.
Eurodollars were steady, unimpressed with the 0.1 percent rise in the U.S. March consumer index, released on Tuesday.
December settled at 93.415 against its IMM close of 93.420. -- Angela Tan, Singapore newsroom (65-8703083)
